content_data.section_title: Systems built to run, not just demo
content_data.section_subtitle: Each service below runs on our own infrastructure first, so what you see here is deployed, not proposed.

items.body: Our Companies House verification pipeline runs area discovery, entity scraping, automated verification and tiered name-matching on active companies. It's checked more than 2,000 business records, with 937 of those enriched with filed accounts data. We run this on our own sites before we ever offer it to a client, so what you see is working, not proposed.
items.hook: Business data is only worth acting on if it's true
items.continuation: so we check every record against a source that doesn't move for anyone

items.body: Workflows are defined in the database and re-read on every message, so a step can change without taking the system down. Some workers spawn their own sub-agents when a task splits further. Our catalogue holds more than 150 agent definitions across site build, design, content, research, quality audit, news and business intelligence, with 74 currently active.
items.hook: One agent can do one job well
items.continuation: but a real workload needs several jobs done in the right order, so a supervisor hands tasks to workers and checks what comes back

items.body: You decide which steps run straight through and which wait for a sign-off. A low-risk step can complete on its own while a step touching money or a public claim stops for a human. It's a control you set, not a promise we make on your behalf.
items.hook: Some steps need a person to say yes before the system carries on
items.continuation: so approval is set per stage, not as a single switch for the whole pipeline

items.body: Our own systems hold more than 2,000 orchestration state records. That log is what lets you check why a system did what it did, weeks after the fact, rather than take our word for it.
items.hook: Every decision an agent makes gets written down
items.continuation: so it can be read back later, not just trusted at the time

items.body: A workflow step can call Claude, Gemini, Mistral or another provider, or run down a self-hosted Ollama path that never leaves the cluster. That distinction matters when a step touches data you don't want handed to a third party.
items.hook: Different steps call for different models
items.continuation: and sometimes for no external provider at all, so routing is set step by step rather than fixed for the whole system

items.body: The multi-source news pipeline refreshes every six hours and scores each item as it arrives. As of our last snapshot it held over 9,545 items collected, with more than 8,297 credibility-scored. The score can still be wrong, which is why we treat it as a signal to check against, not a verdict.
items.hook: News gets published faster than anyone can check it
items.continuation: so we built a pipeline that scores credibility as items come in
